title: Neural Networks Are Already Clean
author: Nick Cammarata, with Curt Tigges on the language-model section (Goodfire)
updated_note: on 30 October a footnote softened the central example ("it's not a cat and car neuron, it's a V-shape neuron" became a neuron that brings cats and cars together because of a shared V shape); by 27 November the companion paper was linked where it had been "forthcoming" and a Prior work list was added; no number changed (compared with the first archived copy of 15 October in Provenance)
takeaway: An essay, with interactive figures but no released code, arguing from case studies that the canonical evidence for superposition in InceptionV1 was misread (the cat-and-car neuron groups a shared V shape; the car-into-dogs circuit is a shared pose, seen through reward-hacked feature visualizations), that most remaining mixing in a neuron is related offshoots it calls recursive generalization, and that squeezing layers of small vision models made neurons coarser rather than mixed. Its language-model numbers are preliminary, agent-assisted audits: about 90% of Qwen3-32B neuron poles with one main job, under thresholds the essay says move the number.
verdict: Believe the diagnosis of the old examples and the method lessons (read both poles, trace the circuit, distrust free feature visualization deep in a network): the author co-wrote the original readings and overturns them with retrained models. Treat the percentages as one team's judgement rather than measurements: the essay publishes no rubric or sample for its 90%, its companion paper measures something narrower on another model (69% of 5,468 poles dominated by one mode), and the absence of superposition is argued from not finding it, under a definition (packing unrelated things) narrower than the field's usual one.

headline.k: in preliminary audits of Qwen3-32B have one main job, often with small related offshoots; about 7% have two related jobs and 2 to 4% are not yet understood
headline.d: agent-assisted; the essay says the threshold for "one thing" moves the number
headline.at: we estimate that roughly 90% of neuron poles

headline.k: InceptionV1's last layer read with 2014-era tools, against a ConvNeXt with the same parameter count and data (the same InceptionV1 is about 50% with better tools, 70% retrained)
headline.d: the author's estimates by inspection; no rubric stated
headline.at: In the ConvNeXt of the same size, it’s about 99%

headline.k: random gallery neurons where examples an agent wrote from the explanation alone beat near misses written to fool it (15 tied, 4 lost)
headline.d: examples fired strongly 76% of the time, near misses 11%, the most distant concept about 1%

discussion.t: LessWrong linkpost (Yair Halberstadt), where most of the expert replies sit

responses.t: Comment on the LessWrong linkpost (crossposted from X)
responses.n: "Interesting work, but I don't think it's a significant update to the big picture." Agrees neuron-based exploratory work (neuron attribution graphs) may be practical, and that it is far easier on a frontier model than training dictionaries; disagrees with "solving interpretability" readings. Still holds superposition is real: more concepts than residual dimensions, and far more memorised facts than neurons, which he expects to sit in weak activations whose ablation would hurt; doubts the vision results transfer; finds the essay's definition of monosemantic too loose.

responses.t: Neural networks are not already clean
responses.n: Accepts the observation that people wrote neurons off as polysemantic too fast. Argues a pattern that fits the top examples is not an explanation: it can miss which inputs of the pattern never fire it (precision against recall) and what the activation magnitudes carry. Proposes simulation scored by downstream KL on a large dataset, which would have flagged "cats and cars" too; reports that in his results ablating small activations substantially degrades models (data not yet shared); raised the Colorado and Tornado neuron as a counterexample.

responses.t: Why Clean Neurons Are Not Enough
responses.by: Goutham Nalagatla and Carlos Guerrero Alvarez (LessWrong)
responses.n: Grants the empirical claim and asks what follows: a coherent abstraction (the bow-tie neuron with its dress shoes and flip-flops) need not have a compact description, and knowing what each neuron responds to is not knowing how they compose into a computation at frontier scale. Asks for a fixed-budget comparison of neuron-based against SAE-based explanations.

Reran OpenAI's 2023 explain-and-simulate method with Claude Opus 5.5 on 50 random GPT-2 XL neurons (layers 8 to 40): about 8% scored 0.8 or more (3 to 19% across his thresholds), against about 0.3% for GPT-4 in 2023; "if clean means every neuron can be explained in a single sentence, GPT-2 XL is not clean." leogao replied that the 2023 method itself should not be replicated.

From someone who worked on neuron-basis interpretability: the agenda is promising, and neurons give an "overlay" of probes and steering handles native to the model; but high activations are probably not expressive enough for gears-level explanation (the wallet graph does not say why honesty connects to the wallet), and steering single neurons worked less well in MoE models.

responses.t: Datasets Determine the Difficulty of Interpretability
responses.n: On the companion paper: the distribution of text a neuron is explained on decides how clean it looks, and interpretability is wanted for behaviour on inputs nobody anticipated, where a corpus-based explanation has not been tested.

since.t: Neurons as an Interpretable Basis (Goodfire, the companion paper)
since.n: Tigges, Kowal, McGrath, Lewis and Cammarata on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (about 5 million neurons): keeping the strongest 320 of 4,096 routed neuron activations per token moves web-text loss from 1.886 to 1.940 (reasoning needs a light fine-tune to recover); 47% of 5,468 neuron poles have one mode and 69% are dominated by one mode; judged descriptions detect firing with 95% accuracy against random text. Its appendix answers the Colorado and Tornado counterexample: about 98.8% of the neuron's effect is places, the Tornado mode is causally real but rare.

since.t: Linkpost: "Neural Networks Are Already Clean" Followup Technical Paper
since.n: Julian Bradshaw's linkpost of the companion paper, with its discussion.

resources.t: Zoom In: An Introduction to Circuits
resources.by: Olah, Cammarata et al., Distill, 2020 (the work the essay revises)
resources.n: Where the cat-and-car neuron and the car-into-dogs circuit were first offered as the two examples of polysemanticity and superposition.
The definition the essay sets aside (more features than dimensions) and the toy world where packing does happen; the essay finds no fault with its experiments, only with how far they transfer.
The informal note whose framing (composition against superposition as strategies) the essay calls closest to its own question.

resources.t: Towards Monosemanticity: Decomposing Language Models With Dictionary Learning
resources.n: The sparse-autoencoder program the essay argues against starting from; its rubric gave the median neuron of a one-layer model 0 of 14.

resources.t: Multimodal Neurons in Artificial Neural Networks
resources.n: CLIP's neurons (the Trump neuron), and the "conjoined features" subsection the essay credits as the first description of recursive generalization.

resources.t: Language Models Can Explain Neurons in Language Models
resources.n: The automated interpretability project behind the 1.7% figure, and the simulation score the essay distrusts.
Labels for the companion paper's neurons, browsable.

kb.n: The nearest neighbour among the articles: an agent editing Qwen3.5-0.8B by reading weights and activations; its edit was directional steering, the same kind of check this essay runs on single neurons.

What a language-model neuron is here: one hidden unit of a block's feed-forward layer, which reads from the residual stream through its input row and writes back through one column of the down projection.
SwiGLU, the gate and value the essay's double-negative regime comes from.
Routers and experts; that page's measured "routing tracks the token, not the topic" sits beside the essay's claim that experts are far more specialised than reported.

kb.t: Topic: llm-architecture, Inside a real model tab
kb.n: The residual stream and attention measured on a real model.
Autoencoders in general; a sparse autoencoder is one with a wide, mostly-zero code trained on a layer's activations.
Qwen3-32B and Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, the models audited.
Kimi K3 (2.8T parameters), where the essay shows a neuron-only attribution graph.

kb.t: Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision (CLIP)
kb.n: The model whose neurons Multimodal Neurons studied, source of the Trump-neuron example.
